eligibility.evidence: Methods and Tables 1-2: ChatGPT 4.0 and 3.5 diagnose 42 clinical vignettes taken from five published bias experiments (salient distracting features, disruptive patients, availability bias; refs 27-31), compared with 265 residents. Cites the human studies, new model responses, accuracy and bias effect analysed.

A.title: Bias Sensitivity in Diagnostic Decision-Making: Comparing ChatGPT with Residents

paradigms.name: Salient distracting features in clinical vignettes (diagnostic bias)
Disruptive versus neutral patient behaviour in clinical vignettes (diagnostic bias)
paradigms.source_paper: Schmidt et al. 2017 (ref 31); Mamede et al. 2017 (ref 27)

paradigms.name: Availability bias from a prior look-alike case (diagnostic bias)
paradigms.source_paper: Mamede et al. 2010 (ref 28); Schmidt et al. 2014 (ref 30)

D.population: Dutch junior residents in internal medicine (202) and family medicine (63), from five earlier published experiments
D.metric: Mean proportion of correct most-likely diagnoses per condition

E.headline: ChatGPT shows bias-induced accuracy drops like residents when bias is part of the case, but is unaffected when the bias is a prior look-alike case.

G.notes: Each vignette set run 50 times, but variance is not reported and chi-square tests are not tied to a model version. Resident data are single published cell means. Vignette text sits in Supplement 1, not seen here (f4 coded no). Prompt-nudging checks are anecdotal, which makes the robustness call weak. GPT-3.5 missing for one experiment.
